title: Integral geometric-fibre reconstruction with projection-normalized restriction maps
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a scheme $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the strict derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $Rf_*$ be the tower direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

For a geometric point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], set $S=X\times_Ys$ with projections $v:S\to X$, $h:S\to s$ [def-pc-base-change], and $P_y=\{x:s\to X\mid fx=y\}$. For $x\in P_y$ let $i_x:s\to S$ be the unique lift, so $vi_x=x$ and $hi_x=\operatorname{id}_s$. This is a finite set; an empty sum indexed by $P_y$ is the zero object. Write $L(-)^*$ for the completed integral pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $(-)_n^*$ for its exact finite-coefficient inverse image.

For every $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ the complexes $Rf_*K$ and $Lv^*K$ are integral constructible, and the canonical finite-reduction comparisons are isomorphisms of derived coefficient systems, including their transition maps:
$$\mathcal R_Y(Rf_*K)\simeq(f_{*,n}K_n)_n,\quad
\mathcal R_S(Lv^*K)\simeq(v_n^*K_n)_n,\quad
\mathcal R_s(Rh_*Lv^*K)\simeq(h_{*,n}v_n^*K_n)_n.$$
Here $\mathcal R_W$ sends an integral complex to its strict derived reduction system, formed on one flat-term K-flat representative. Every displayed comparison is the counit of the derived reduction/total-limit adjunction, whose component is the scalar-extension adjoint of the actual limit projection; these are comparisons of systems, rather than separately chosen level isomorphisms. Use the coefficient-system category and counit specified in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

The level exchange and counit-germ arrows
$$b_n:y_n^*f_{*,n}K_n\to h_{*,n}v_n^*K_n,\qquad
r_n:h_{*,n}v_n^*K_n\to\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}x_n^*K_n,$$
formed on strict quotients as above, induce specified natural isomorphisms in $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$
$$b_K:Ly^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*Lv^*K,\qquad
r_K:Rh_*Lv^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}Lx^*K.$$
Their total-limit projections are the preceding level arrows under the canonical system comparisons. In the strict Roos model $R\varprojlim C_n=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nC_n\to\prod_nC_n)[-1]$, the comparison
$$R\varprojlim_n\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}\operatorname{Res}_n x_n^*K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n x_n^*K_n$$
is the coordinate reindexing of products, with the same $1-s$, cone differentials and projections; it is the finite biproduct comparison. The empty-index comparison is the unique isomorphism between zero objects. These assertions are made in the derived category before applying point sections; no interchange of a point inverse image with an arbitrary inverse limit is asserted.

source.place: Bhatt–Scholze Section 3.5, Lemma 3.5.7, and Section 6.7, Lemma 6.7.2; derived reduction-system reconstruction and finite Roos biproduct comparison, returned steps 6–7.

proof.text: Put $F=(f_{*,n}K_n)_n$ on $Y$ and $V=(v_n^*K_n)_n$ on $S$. The finite completed-image comparison gives $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, with canonical reduction maps $(Rf_*K)_n\to F_n$ invertible. Integral pullback preservation gives $Lv^*K\in D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_E)$. The coherent pullback-system comparison identifies $\mathcal R_S(Lv^*K)$ with $V$, at every level by the scalar adjoint of the actual Roos projection. Thus this is the counit $e_V$, rather than a choice of unrelated level identifications. These results apply because $f$ is finite between the stipulated separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $v$ is a scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.7 (reduction/limit adjunction), Lemmas 6.5.9(5), 6.5.11(3), 6.7.2; specialization to finite geometric fibres of the blueprint finite-stalk paragraph.

proof.text: In the derived system category form the actual counit $e_F:\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_YF\to F$. The tower-direct-image definition identifies $\mathcal L_YF=Rf_*K$. By the coefficient calculus its evaluation is the scalar adjoint of the limit projection, exactly the canonical reduction map in Step 1. Every evaluation is invertible, so the calculus makes $e_F$ invertible as a system map, including quotient transitions. This proves the first displayed system comparison. It uses conservative evaluation only to detect invertibility of an already constructed map.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.7 (reduction/limit adjunction), Lemmas 6.5.9(5), 6.5.11(3), 6.7.2; specialization to finite geometric fibres of the blueprint finite-stalk paragraph.

proof.text: The completed-image result also applies to the finite base change $h:S\to s$. Apply it to $Lv^*K$ from Step 1. It makes $Rh_*Lv^*K$ integral constructible and its canonical reduction counit invertible at every evaluation. By the same conservative-evaluation argument the counit is invertible as a system map. Compose it with $h_{*,\bullet}(e_V)$, using the coherent comparison of Step 1. The result identifies $\mathcal R_s(Rh_*Lv^*K)$ with $C=(h_{*,n}v_n^*K_n)_n$. Naturality of the reduction/limit counit identifies this composite with $e_C$: its component is adjoint to the actual projection to $C_n$. Thus the third comparison has the required normalization and transition maps.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.7 (reduction/limit adjunction), Lemmas 6.5.9(5), 6.5.11(3), 6.7.2; specialization to finite geometric fibres of the blueprint finite-stalk paragraph.

proof.text: Use one flat-term K-flat representative of $K$. The strict counit-restriction theorem supplies $B=(y_n^*f_{*,n}K_n)_n\xrightarrow{b}C\xrightarrow{r}D=(\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}x_n^*K_n)_n$ as actual natural derived-system maps, represented by quotient-compatible chain maps; both are levelwise quasi-isomorphisms. It also supplies finiteness of $P_y$ and the empty-fibre convention. Their restricted total limits are therefore specified natural isomorphisms. The tower pullback definition gives $Ly^*Rf_*K=\mathcal L_s(y_\bullet^*\mathcal R_Y(Rf_*K))$. Applying $\mathcal L_s y_\bullet^*$ to $e_F$ identifies this object with $\mathcal L_sB$. Step 3 and the direct-image definition identify $Rh_*Lv^*K$ with $\mathcal L_sC$. Define $b_K$ by these identifications and $\mathcal L_s(b)$. This proves the first fibre isomorphism without pulling $y^*$ through an inverse limit.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.7 (reduction/limit adjunction), Lemmas 6.5.9(5), 6.5.11(3), 6.7.2; specialization to finite geometric fibres of the blueprint finite-stalk paragraph.

proof.text: For the strict chain comparison, only existence of countable products is needed. The functor taking a tower to its product is additive by product extensionality. The proved two-coordinate formula for the actual integralOperationsRoosFunctor map (the private roosMap_coordinates helper of the ambient-operation module) and mappingCocone.id_X show that this functor is additive too. Mathlib then makes both canonical finite-biproduct comparisons invertible. The product comparison is the map alpha whose (x,n) projection is pr_n followed by the x projection. The strict tower projection commutes with 1-s by integralOperationsRoos_square; composing the Roos map with mappingCocone.fst and pr_n gives the displayed level projection. For an empty point set the target biproduct is zero by projection extensionality, the isomorphism makes the source zero, and uniqueness of maps out of zero identifies every proposed isomorphism with the specified map. Countable product exactness and the normalized derived Roos comparison are still used by the unfinished reconstruction argument, but are not needed for this strict finite-coordinate theorem.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; elementary finite-coordinate reindexing of its product/cone model.

proof.text: Define $r_K$ as the composite $Rh_*Lv^*K\simeq\mathcal L_sC\xrightarrow{\mathcal L_s(r)}\mathcal L_sD\simeq\bigoplus_x\mathcal L_s(x_n^*K_n)_n$. The first arrow is Step 3, the middle arrow is the specified strict counit-germ map of Step 4, and the last is exactly Step 5. By the definition of completed pullback each last summand is $Lx^*K$. All arrows are invertible. The pullback-preservation theorem makes these summands integral constructible; alternatively the resulting finite sum is isomorphic to the integral constructible object $Rh_*Lv^*K$. Thus both fibre arrows lie in the full integral constructible category.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.7 (reduction/limit adjunction), Lemmas 6.5.9(5), 6.5.11(3), 6.7.2; specialization to finite geometric fibres of the blueprint finite-stalk paragraph.

proof.text: Finally the total-limit projection is natural for a strict map of towers. Applied to $b$ and $r$, this gives $\pi_n\mathcal L_s(b)=\operatorname{Res}_n(b_n)\pi_n$ and $\pi_n\mathcal L_s(r)=\operatorname{Res}_n(r_n)\pi_n$. The normalized Roos comparison preserves these projections, and Step 5 preserves every $(x,n)$ coordinate. Conjugating these equations by the counit system comparisons of Steps 1–3 gives exactly the projection identities claimed for $b_K$ and $r_K$. Naturality follows from naturality of the counits, strict fibre maps, and coordinate reindexing. All constructions took place over $s$ in derived categories before taking any sections.
